decisions.decision: UC1 classified as confirmed flow: Salesforce → QuickBooks invoice creation
decisions.rationale: Explicitly stated in Apr 28 transcript: agreement creation in Salesforce triggers invoice creation in QuickBooks. Multiple speakers confirmed this as the intended automation.
decisions.evidence: when an agreement is created in Salesforce, it will generate a new invoice in QuickBooks for an existing account

decisions.decision: UC2 classified as confirmed flow: QuickBooks → Salesforce payment/invoice status sync
decisions.rationale: Crystal Robinson confirmed the manual process (entering QB invoice number, date, open balance back into SF Agreement custom fields). The integration scope explicitly requires automating this sync.
decisions.evidence: track payment updates from QuickBooks to Salesforce, including the open balance... update the number, amount, dates

decisions.decision: UC3 classified as confirmed flow: Excel/Google Sheets → Salesforce inventory sync
decisions.rationale: AE transcript and Holly's written answers confirm inventory data (titles, quantities, cost) should flow from spreadsheets into a Salesforce custom inventory object. Both Holly and Maria aligned on this.
decisions.evidence: push the data directly um and the details directly from Excel in real time or from QuickBooks if it's living in QuickBooks. And so then we can push that inventory data directly into Salesforce

decisions.decision: UC4 classified as confirmed flow: QuickBooks → Salesforce inventory/product cost data
decisions.rationale: Maria confirmed some inventory data lives in QuickBooks and should be visible in Salesforce dashboards. AE scope doc explicitly includes 'Extract inventory data from Excel / QuickBooks → Salesforce'. Kept separate from UC3 because data source is QuickBooks not Excel.
decisions.evidence: Maria Gonzalez-Pettway: some of this lives in QuickBooks... she's going to have to select it on the invoice or it's going to populate Salesforce... and now it's going to start to discount it out of our inventory

decisions.decision: UC5 classified as potential flow: product/title master data sync between QB and Salesforce
decisions.rationale: Team explicitly deferred this in May 8 call. 'The strategy for maintaining product titles across QuickBooks and Salesforce is placed on hold pending input from Maria.' A gap exists: without sync, title lists will diverge.
decisions.evidence: Product title maintenance process deferred — the strategy for maintaining product titles across QuickBooks and Salesforce is placed on hold pending input from Maria

decisions.decision: UC6 classified as potential flow: CCR fulfillment flag — Salesforce must know when pre-agreement fulfillment occurs
decisions.rationale: Holly's written answers describe CCR (Contract Change Request) items where fulfillment happens before agreement is formally closed. 'The system needs to know that when the agreement comes in, it has already been fulfilled.' This implies a fulfillment-state sync not addressed elsewhere.
decisions.evidence: Sales will ask us to ship materials ahead of a closed/won agreement. This happens on a CCR — if/when approved, they are treated as closed/won business and are added to our fulfillment queue. The system needs to know that when the agreement comes in, it has already been fulfilled.

decisions.decision: UC7 classified as potential flow: QB inventory decrement sync to Salesforce
decisions.rationale: Holly tracks inventory decrements daily as fulfillment occurs. If QB is inventory master post-integration, decrement events need to propagate to Salesforce inventory object to keep dashboard accurate. Not confirmed as a separate automated flow — could be covered by UC4 on a scheduled basis.
decisions.evidence: Each order decrements our existing inventory. I run a daily/weekly report to look for any potential shortages.

decisions.decision: QuickBooks connector key set to null — P0 unresolved: Online vs Desktop not confirmed
decisions.rationale: Both quickbooks-online and quickbooks-enterprise exist in connector-names.json. These are incompatible integration paths. Transcript says 'QuickBooks' without version specification. FK-020 (verified) confirms these cannot be conflated.
decisions.evidence: QuickBooks mentioned throughout without version qualifier. connector-names.json has separate entries for quickbooks-online and quickbooks-enterprise.

decisions.decision: Excel connector key set to null — file storage location unconfirmed
decisions.rationale: Holly said 'spreadsheets I own or Google Sheets' — both are possible. Local Excel files cannot be accessed from CloudHub 2.0. microsoft-excel-online requires SharePoint/OneDrive. google-sheets is a separate connector.
decisions.evidence: if it starts out in spreadsheets I own or Google Sheets (Holly Wale, AE transcript 00:03:16)

decisions.decision: P0 raised for QuickBooks version — must resolve before architecture can proceed
decisions.rationale: Two incompatible connector paths exist. Architecture decisions for UC1, UC2, UC4 all depend on this. Cannot proceed to Vera or Flo steps until client confirms QB product.
decisions.evidence: quickbooks-online vs quickbooks-enterprise in connector-names.json; FK-020 verified across 1+ projects

decisions.decision: P0 raised for Excel/Google Sheets file storage location — CloudHub 2.0 ephemeral filesystem constraint
decisions.rationale: CloudHub 2.0 cannot read local filesystem paths. If Holly's Excel files are on a local machine, they must be migrated to cloud storage before MuleSoft can access them. Connector selection depends on where files live.
decisions.evidence: CloudHub 2.0 local filesystem is ephemeral (PLANNING_CONTEXT.md Critical Notes); Holly said 'spreadsheets I own or Google Sheets' — no cloud location confirmed

decisions.decision: Flag raised for Salesforce State/Country Picklists — affects ISBN logic table design
decisions.rationale: The configurable ISBN lookup table maps state + school → ISBN. If State/Country Picklists are enabled, state values are ISO codes, not names. Logic table format must match. Classified as flag (not P0) because it affects data format, not whether integration is possible.
decisions.evidence: Kailash Chanda suggested building a configurable logic table in Salesforce to automate the lookup of the correct ISBN based on state and school

decisions.decision: Industry vertical set to educational publishing / EdTech — not a standard BMAD vertical slug
decisions.rationale: AgileMind sells curriculum to K-12 districts. No canonical vertical slug exists for educational publishing. Closest standard model is commerce (OAGIS 10.x) for order/invoice flows. Will need canonical-extensions.yaml for education-specific fields.
decisions.evidence: AgileMind sells educational programs (print + digital) to school districts... products are sold by academic year
